newsitem.title: USA: Initial, Hollis sign definite merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Initial, Hollis sign definite merger pact.

text.p: Initial Acquisition Corp said on Monday it signed a definitive merger agreement with Hollis-Eden Inc, a biopharmaceutical company which develops and commercializes therapeutic and preventative agents to treat viral and immune disorders.
An agreement to merge was announced on November 6.
Hollis would merge into Initial Acquisition, and the name of the new company would be changed to Hollis-Eden Pharmaceuticals Inc, the company said.
One share of the surviving company would be issued for each outstanding share of Hollis held, the company said.

All outstanding Hollis-Eden warrants and options would be converted into options and warrants of the surviving company, Initial said. The surviving company would therefore issue 4,911,004 shares of common stock as well as 2,229,650 options and warrants, Initial said.

As a provision of the merger, each Initial holder, who had the right to have stock redeemed in lieu of participating in the merger, would receive additional shares two years after the merger closed if the average public trading price for Hollis-Eden Pharmaceuticals Inc did not equal or exceed $20 per share for a specified period of time within those two years, the company said.

Richard Hollis, chairman of Hollis-Eden, would become chairman, president and chief executive officer of the surviving corporation, and Salvatore Zizza, Initial's chairman, would be a director of the surviving company, Initial said.
Hollis-Eden said it believed its initial drug discovery, INACTIVIN, had the potential to be a safe, efficacious and cost-effective strategy in the treatment of HIV/AIDS.
The company said it expected to enter Phase II trials with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on INACTIVIN upon completion of the merger with Initial Acquisition.
